pairs.subject: data-access
pairs.evidence: scripts/data-analysis/kg-repair-orphans.ts:43 The orphan repair still opens PGlite directly and issues its own copy of the archive-then-delete SQL against kg_edge, even though store.deleteKgEdges exists. That puts a kg_edge writer outside the repository, and the file's header comment (line 12) wrongly says the delete goes through the store.

techniques.evidence: scripts/data-analysis/kg-repair-orphans.ts:43 Raw connection plus a hand-copied archive+delete statement in a script. The comment at lines 22-25 admits the bypass ('kept byte-compatible'). Every other writer in this context goes through getStore().

scripts/data-analysis/kg-compute.ts:375 The --reset rebuild runs as three separately committed transactions: clearKg (kg.ts:440), upsertKgNodes (kg.ts:305), upsertKgEdges (kg.ts:333). If a write fails after the clear, the graph is left durably cleared or half-rebuilt. The script does exit 1 and history keeps the archive, but no single boundary covers the replace-the-graph invariant.
scripts/data-analysis/kg-repair-orphans.ts:90 Even the bypassing statement binds its values as $1..$3. The interpolated identifiers come from the KG_EDGE_COLS constant, not from input.

scripts/data-analysis/kg-repair-orphans.ts:32 The column set is taken from the one mapper declaration rather than retyped. The other writers receive typed KgNodeRow/KgEdgeRow from the store. Caveat: kg-repair-orphans types its own rows with ad-hoc generics (line 46).
scripts/data-analysis/kg-compute.ts:122 Inputs are read as whole sets per term and written in chunked bulk upserts. One minor exception: kg-repair-orphans deletes in a per-key loop (line 78).
scripts/data-analysis/kg-writer-provenance.test.ts:27 Writer provenance and prop-merge are tested against a real PGlite copy of the test template, not a mock.
